transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep losing a lot of time checking things over and over. I’ll reread emails and texts, reopen folders, and replay conversations in my head before I leave the house or try to start work. It feels like I need to make sure I didn’t make some serious mistake.
What happens inside you if you try to stop yourself from checking?

I feel like I can’t settle until I’ve gone back over it. I start worrying I may have missed some serious mistake, so I reread the email or text, reopen the folder, or replay what I said. Before I know it, a lot of time has gone by.
Deep down, do you feel that this checking is excessive or unreasonable, or does it feel like the right and sensible way to do things?
Part of me knows I’m spending too much time on it, but it still feels necessary in the moment. I keep rereading or going back over things because I need to be sure I didn’t make some serious mistake.
Besides worrying about making mistakes, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other everyday matters, like health, finances, or family?
I’m not sure I’d say I’m constantly worried about lots of different things. It’s mainly the worry about whether I made a mistake.
Do these doubts and urges to check feel like intrusive, unwanted thoughts popping into your head against your will?

Yes. They pop in when I’m trying to focus on something else—like working through a system design or preparing a lesson. I’ll suddenly think I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, mishandled family photos, or let someone in the community down. I know I’ve already gone over it, but I can’t seem to just let the thought pass.
